manual:
Controls the priority order the Integration Service Supervisor uses when available Home RAM can't start every eligible service at once - move services up or down to decide which ones win limited capacity first.

Each row shows the service entry script's own RAM and, when declared, a separate Children figure. Child costs come from the integration's placement-independent capacity list, so a worker remains visible after moving from Home to another rooted RAM host without ordinary payload scripts being mistaken for fixed children.

The Combined total figure above the list is a capacity-planning ceiling, not a live snapshot: every listed service plus its declared children, summed, regardless of whether each one (or an optional sub-toggle inside it) is currently switched on or where a child will run. This is different from what's actually consuming Home RAM right now - see Home Server's own Service Startup RAM Limit for that.
